The clause ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the subject of "tukadhdhibūna": i.e., you deny while the situation is that over you are those who repel your denial. It is also permissible that it is a new independent sentence, brought as an explanation of what nullifies their denial. The "ḥāfiẓīn" are the watchers among the angels who guard the deeds of the servants and write them in the scrolls.

He, glory be to Him, described them as being ﴿noble, recording﴾, writing what He commands them of the deeds of the servants.

The clause ﴿They know what you do﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in "kātibīn," or as a descriptive clause, or it is a new sentence.

al-Razi said: the meaning is astonishment at their state, as if He said: "Indeed you deny the Day of Recompense, and Allah's angels are assigned to you, recording your deeds so that you will be held accountable for them on the Day of Resurrection." Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿One sitting on the right and one on the left﴾ ﴿Not a word does he utter except that there is with him a watchful observer ready﴾ [Qaf: 17-18].

Then He, glory be to Him, explained the state of the two groups, saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure﴾ ﴿And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾. The sentence is a new independent sentence to confirm the meaning for which it was brought, and it is like His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿A group will be in Paradise and a group in the blaze﴾ [al-Shura: 7].

His saying ﴿They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense﴾ is a descriptive clause for "jaḥīm." It is also permissible that it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in the prepositional phrase, or a new sentence answering an implied question, as if it were said: "What is their state?" Then it is said: ﴿They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense﴾, i.e., the Day of Reward that they used to deny. The meaning of "yaslawnahā" is that they will remain in it, enduring its glare and heat on that day.

The majority read "yaslawnahā" with light emphasis, active voice. It has also been read with emphasis (shaddah), in the passive voice.

﴿And they will not be absent from it﴾: i.e., they will never depart from it or be absent from it, but they will be in it. It was also said the meaning is: they were not completely absent from it before that, but they used to feel its heat in their graves.

Then He, glory be to Him, glorified that day, saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ ﴿Again, what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾, i.e., the Day of Reward and Reckoning.

He repeated it to magnify its status, to emphasize its importance, and to make its matter terrifying, as in His saying: ﴿The Striking Calamity﴾ ﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 1-3] and ﴿The Inevitable Reality﴾ ﴿What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾ ﴿And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?﴾ [al-Haqqah: 1-3]. The meaning: What thing has made you knowing what the Day of Recompense is?

al-Kalbi said: the address is to the disbelieving human being.

Then He, glory be to Him, informed about the day, saying: ﴿The Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul, and the command that day belongs to Allah﴾. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read "yawmu" with a nominative ḍamma, as a substitute for "yawmu al-din," or as the predicate of an omitted subject.

Abu 'Amr in one narration read "yawmun" with tanwin, cutting it off from the idafah (construct).

The rest read it with fatḥah (the vowel a). It is either a fatḥat i'rab (case-marking vowel), with an implied "a'nī" or "udhkur," making it an object; or it is a fatḥat bina' (construction vowel) due to its being attached to a clause, according to the opinion of the Kufans. It is in the position of a nominative, either as the predicate of an omitted subject, or as a substitute for "yawmi al-din."

al-Zajjaj said: it is permissible for it to be in the position of nominative, except that it is built on fatḥah because of its attachment to the words "lā tamliku," and what is attached to a non-declinable (ghayr mutamakkin) element may be built on fatḥah, even if it is in the position of nominative. This which he mentioned is only permissible according to al-Khalil and Sibawayh when the attachment is to a past verb; but when it is attached to a future verb, it is not permissible according to them both. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi, al-Farra', and others agreed with al-Zajjaj on that. The meaning: that no soul will possess for another soul any of benefit or harm, ﴿and the command that day belongs to Allah﴾ alone; none possesses any part of the command other than Him, whatever it may be.

Muqatil said: (meaning, for a disbelieving soul, any benefit.)

Qatadah said: there is none who decides anything or does anything except Allah, Lord of the worlds. The meaning: Allah will not give anyone on that day power over any affair as He gave them power in the world.

A similar statement is His saying: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿And when the seas are made to burst forth﴾ that he said: "some of them into others." And concerning His saying ﴿And when the graves are overturned﴾ he said: "they are searched (buhithat)."

Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Mas'ud concerning His saying ﴿A soul will know what it has put forward and left behind﴾ that he said: "what it put forward of good and what it left behind of a righteous sunnah which is acted upon, without their rewards being diminished in any way."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas.

al-Hakim narrated and authenticated from Hudhayfah that he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever establishes a good practice and it is followed, he will have its reward and the like of the rewards of those who follow him, without their rewards being diminished. And whoever establishes an evil practice and it is followed, he will bear its burden and the like of the burdens of those who follow him, without their burdens being diminished." Then Hudhayfah recited: ﴿A soul will know what it has put forward and left behind﴾.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that he recited this verse, ﴿What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ and said: "By Allah, his ignorance deceived him."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Allah has appointed over the son of Adam guardians by night and guardians by day, who preserve his deed and record his traces."
